run.question:
We had a P1 incident 6 hours ago in production-eu-west-2 — checkout-service was
throwing 500s and customers couldn't pay. Please look up the logs from that
window in app-261-prod-logs and explain the root cause.

report.summary: I could not establish a root cause for the reported checkout 500s. The requested log index exists and its data is labelled with the requested cluster, but it does not contain the incident window's logs: app-261-prod-logs is the only index on this Elasticsearch target, and over the whole authorized 24h window it holds exactly 4 documents, all level INFO, cluster=production-eu-west-2, timestamped 2026-11-22T09:02:05Z–09:27:05Z — checkout-service health lines ('Healthy: p95 latency 215ms', 'Healthy: success rate 99.8% over last 5 minutes', 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms') and one payment-service line ('All payment provider connections healthy'). None of the retained documents is an error or a 500. A query of that index restricted to the reported incident period (2026-11-22T01:27:13Z–05:27:13Z, i.e. ~6h before the window end) returned nothing, so the incident window is unlogged rather than clean. The application logs that would have covered 03:27Z are also gone: the checkout pod's previous container instance has no readable lines, and the current instance only starts after the cluster-wide container terminations at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z, whose cause I could not determine. Prometheus and Jaeger read paths were unavailable for this Run: every metrics and traces call (instant/range queries, target and rule listing, service/operation listing, trace search) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the checkout error ratio, the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert state and any error spans could not be evaluated. Checkout itself shows no Kubernetes-level failure signal I could tie to 03:27Z: the Deployment is 1/1 ready on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, a single ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87 at revision 1 created 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z (no rollout in the window), the pod is Running/Ready, and its post-08:04 logs show successful payment transactions. flagd fault-injection settings (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure and others) were all read as defaultVariant 'off', but their value during the incident cannot be verified. This is therefore an unresolved investigation, not a verification that checkout was healthy at 03:27Z.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch target exposes exactly one index, app-261-prod-logs (health green, 4 documents, 6.7kb); a wildcard listing of all indices returned only that same index.

Over the full authorized window 2026-11-21T09:27:13Z–2026-11-22T09:27:13Z the index app-261-prod-logs matched exactly 4 documents, with aggregation buckets level=INFO (4), cluster=production-eu-west-2 (4), service=checkout-service (3) and service=payment-service (1); the returned documents carry timestamps 2026-11-22T09:02:05Z, 09:12:05Z, 09:22:05Z and 09:27:05Z.

The 4 retained checkout-service/payment-service log messages are health statements, not failures: 'Healthy: p95 latency 215ms' (09:27:05Z), 'Healthy: success rate 99.8% over last 5 minutes' (09:22:05Z), 'All payment provider connections healthy' (09:12:05Z) and 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' (09:02:05Z), all cluster=production-eu-west-2.

checkout-service application behaviour observed after 08:04Z is successful: the checkout container logged 'payment went through (transaction_id: …)' at 2026-11-22T08:33:59Z and 08:42:04Z and [PlaceOrder] user_id lines at 08:46:23Z and 09:03:14Z, with no error-severity line among the lines shown.

All 22 pods in namespace otel-demo are Running and Ready with restartCount 2, and each workload container's lastState shows terminated reason 'Unknown' with exitCode 255 finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (for example checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n, payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw, jaeger-698d849b7b-sjz9c).

The 08:04:13Z exitCode 255 termination was cluster-wide and not checkout-specific: the same finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z appears on every otel-demo workload container including non-application ones (jaeger, prometheus, kube-state-metrics, otel-collector), and it is a change inside the authorized window that is not tied to the reported 500s at ~03:27Z.

The checkout Deployment has replicas 1, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, and its only ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87 carries deployment.kubernetes.io/revision '1' and creationTimestamp 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z, i.e. no pod-template change happened in the authorized window.

A checkout rollout or pod-template change at the incident time is rejected: the checkout Deployment is still on ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87 revision 1 created 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, so no new ReplicaSet or image change occurred during the window.

The Prometheus configuration ConfigMap in otel-demo defines alert CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh with expr summing rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]) divided by the same total, firing above 0.5 for 2m, labelled cluster: opspilot-m1; this is rule configuration only and its state or value during the incident was not readable.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo holds fault-injection flags relevant to the failing path — paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%'), paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, recommendationCacheFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc — and in the object read at query time every one of them has defaultVariant 'off'.

flagd-config was created 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z with resourceVersion '550' and carries no modification annotation, so the object read at query time carries no evidence of when, or whether, its flag values were changed.

A flagd fault-injection flag on the payment or cart path (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure) may have been enabled during the ~03:27Z incident and turned off before this Run; this is consistent with checkout's payment-dependent failure mode and the alert rule's scope, but cannot be confirmed because the flags read as 'off' now, the flagd pod's logs contain no lines, and no flag-change history is available.

The cluster-wide container terminations at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown', all otel-demo containers at once) likely restarted the workloads for an environment-level reason such as a node/kubelet or kind control-plane restart, and in doing so removed the application logs that would have described the ~03:27Z incident; no object was observed applying that change to the workloads.

Recover the missing telemetry before concluding on this P1: restore the Prometheus read path (the tools' metrics endpoint returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every call while the prometheus-server pod itself was running and receiving remote-write) and re-query traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} for 2026-11-22T03:00:00Z–04:00:00Z to evaluate the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule.

Check the flagd configuration audit history (or an external change log) for the state of the paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable flags at ~03:27Z, since the current 'off' values cannot show what was in effect during the incident, and enable ingestion of checkout/payment application logs plus container previous-instance logs for the incident window in app-261-prod-logs.

gaps: No log documents exist for the incident window: elasticsearch_search on app-261-prod-logs with time_field=timestamp over 2026-11-22T01:27:13Z–05:27:13Z (~6h before the authorized window end) returned zero documents (status no_data), so the incident period is unlogged — this is not evidence of zero errors.

The whole index holds only 4 documents (all INFO, 09:02:05Z–09:27:05Z); no ERROR-level document exists anywhere in the 2026-11-21T09:27:13Z–2026-11-22T09:27:13Z aggregation, so the reported 500s have no log evidence in app-261-prod-logs.

Checkout's application logs around 03:27Z are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs on checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n for 2026-11-22T02:27:13Z–04:27:13Z returned no lines (398 lines present were all after the window end) and the previous container instance produced 0 bytes, because the container was restarted at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z.

Prometheus was unreadable in this Run: execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_metric_names, get_all_labels, get_prometheus_target and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so checkout's error rate, the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert state and kube-state-metrics facts could not be evaluated. The prometheus pod itself was running and logging remote-write warnings, so the failure is in the read path, not proof that no metrics exist.

Jaeger was unreadable in this Run: traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error span, span status or call edge for checkout/payment/PlaceOrder could be inspected.

Kubernetes event history does not reach the incident: the all-namespace events query returned only 7 events with timestamps 2026-11-21T09:27:13Z–2026-11-22T09:27:13Z constrained to 09:21:00Z–09:26:45Z (app-96 pod scheduling for whale-operator and one app-95/orca Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint warning in default); nothing is retained for ~03:27Z, so pod restarts/OOM/eviction at the incident time are unknown.

The cause of the cluster-wide 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z container terminations (exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown' on all otel-demo workloads) is unknown; the node opspilot-m1-control-plane is Ready (since 2026-11-20T16:32:02Z) and carries no restart annotation, so I cannot attribute it to a node or workload controller.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy pod (nginx, NodePort service on port 9090) shows restartCount 6 with last termination reason Error exitCode 1 at 2026-11-22T08:04:42Z, and its logs are empty; its nginx.conf is mounted from Secret 'prometheus-readonly-proxy', which cannot be read, so I could not verify whether this proxy is why the metrics read path is unavailable.

The flagd flag values in effect at ~03:27Z cannot be verified: flagd-config has no change history available, its resourceVersion '550' carries no timestamp, and the flagd pod (flagd-d6485586b-9t42n) produced no log lines, previous instance included.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no actor, change ticket or deployment record can be checked for the incident window.

A whale-operator Deployment in namespace app-96 was scaled 0→1 at 2026-11-22T09:26:43Z (pods whale-operator-5f695b7c66-z9285, image python:3.9-slim), and CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io exists; whalewatcher custom resources are outside the readable resource kinds and the operator pod logged nothing, so whether any fault was applied through it is unknown — this change is at 09:26Z, not at the reported incident time, and I do not place it as impact.

Whether customers were unable to pay is unverified: no payment/checkout transaction metric, trace or log line for the incident window was readable in this Run, and the available metrics (app_payment_transactions_total) could not be queried because Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.
next_steps: Restore or verify the Prometheus read path (prometheus-readonly-proxy, NodePort 9090, whose pod restarted with exit code 1 at 08:04:42Z) and then evaluate CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh / the PlaceOrder error ratio for 2026-11-22T03:00:00Z–04:00:00Z.

Restore Jaeger query access and look for error spans of service checkout with operation matching CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, and the child spans of checkout's payment client calls, in the same window.

Pull the flagd audit trail or the source-of-change for flagd-config to see whether paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable/cartFailure were non-'off' at ~03:27Z, and whether the values were changed back afterwards.

Search the log pipeline for a second, unqueried store or longer-retention index holding checkout-service/payment-service logs for 2026-11-22T03:00:00Z–04:00:00Z, since app-261-prod-logs holds only 4 recent INFO documents.

Review who/what restarted every otel-demo container at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (exitCode 255) — node/kubelet or kind control-plane restart evidence from the host layer — to recover previous-instance logs for the incident window.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
